title: How to Make Infused Butter | The Bridge
description: A careful small-batch cannabis butter for adults: decarb, low heat, strain, label, lock. Why you can't know the strength, and how to test it slowly.
lede: The base of nearly every homemade edible. It takes an afternoon and a thermometer, and the label and the lockbox matter more than the stove.
html:
Read this all the way through before you buy the butter. The cooking is easy. The hard part is that no lab will ever test what comes off your stove, so every safety decision lands on you. This recipe is for adults 21 and older, at home. You may share with another adult for free within the legal limits. Selling it without a license is illegal.

Ingredients

  • 3.5 grams cannabis flower (an eighth)
  • 1 cup unsalted butter (2 sticks)
  • 1 cup water

You'll also need: a sheet pan, parchment, foil, an oven thermometer, an instant-read thermometer, a small saucepan, cheesecloth, a heatproof bowl, a small jar with a lid, a label and a lockbox.

Method

  1. Heat the oven to 240°F and confirm it with the oven thermometer.
  2. Break the flower up by hand onto parchment on the sheet pan. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. This is decarboxylation, the step that turns THCA into THC. Let it cool with the foil on.
  3. Melt the butter with the water in the saucepan over your lowest heat. The water helps keep the butter from scorching.
  4. Stir in the flower. Hold the mixture between 160°F and 190°F for 2 hours, stirring now and then. It should never boil.
  5. Line a strainer with cheesecloth, set it over the bowl and pour. Press gently. Squeezing hard pushes more plant taste into the butter.
  6. Refrigerate the bowl until the butter sets in a solid layer on top of the water. Lift it off and pat it dry.
  7. Pack the butter into the jar and label it before it goes anywhere: CONTAINS THC, ADULTS ONLY, today's date.

How strong is it? You don't know

There's only one piece of math available, and it gives you a ceiling, not a dose. Grams of flower, times 10, times the Total THC percent on your flower's label, equals the most THC the batch could possibly hold. At 3.5 grams and 20%, that's 700 milligrams across the whole cup. A cup is 48 teaspoons, so up to about 15 milligrams per teaspoon.

The real number will be lower, and it won't be even through the batch. For scale, New York limits a serving of store-bought edible to 10 milligrams of THC and says a new consumer may want to start at 2.5 to 5.

Testing a new batch

Start with a quarter teaspoon, on a day with nothing to do and nowhere to drive. Even at that ceiling, that's under 4 milligrams. Then wait. The state says edibles may take up to two hours to feel and four or more hours to be fully felt, and effects can last 4 to 12 hours. No second helping that day. Keep in mind that fat can raise THC exposure: in one rat study, lipids increased it about 2.5 times. Write down what you took and how it went.

Keeping it safe

Butter looks like butter. That's the whole danger: one unlabeled block in the fridge, and somebody makes toast. The Department of Health says infused products should never sit in a shared fridge or pantry near other food, and the state wants them locked. So use a lockbox, kept apart from the food. Use the butter within a week or freeze it, still locked. If kids live in the house and you can't guarantee that, don't make this.

Spent flower and the leftover water count as cannabis waste. The state's disposal sheet says to mix it with something like coffee grounds or kitty litter, seal it in a container and put it in the regular trash. Don't pour it down the sink.

If anyone eats this by accident, call the Poison Center at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 in an emergency. If it's a pet, call your vet right away.
